headline: The large gains in the literature come from templated benchmarks, from an LLM at runtime, or from token counts that ignore prompt caching; on our held-out traces the largest learnable, hook-deliverable ceiling is stopping after the post-edit green test (17.8% of $ on Haiku, 3.1% on Sonnet 5), then insertion-time Read windowing (14.8% / 4.7%). The dead-end family Adage exploits today is capped at about 2%, and localisation at about 5.6%.
metric_name: oracle share of session $ removable (cumulative-context cost model, provider usage, held-out control sessions)

cache_ttl_5m_instead_of_1h.note: config, not learning; 1h writes at 2x, no inter-request gap > 5 min in 6,519 gaps

leave_one_repo_out: not applicable (ceilings, no learner); per-repo termination ceiling on Haiku: attrs 0.19, click 0.22, marshmallow 0.23, urfave-cli 0.12, vue-core 0.09
vs_baseline: The current system (U11 + learned reflexes, about +1.0 S-hat calls/session post-hoc, +2.11 pre-emptive, roughly 3-6% of $) sits in a family whose total oracle ceiling is about 2% of $ by token accounting (plus the recovery exploration it avoids). The termination and Read-windowing levers have ceilings 7-9x larger on Haiku, but only 1.5-2.5x larger on Sonnet 5.
hard_coded_parts: tail_after_green.py: test-runner regex and pass/fail output signatures (measurement instrument only; E1 must learn the goal event from Drain templates of outputs)
call_anatomy.py: uses evals/lab/normalize.py's hand-written action names (instrument)
localise.py: code-file extension list; task src_files as evaluation labels
cost_anatomy.py: Claude Code's is_error flag; edit = Edit/Write/MultiEdit tool names
ceiling: Haiku 4.5: termination after the post-edit green test 17.8% of $ (all requests after the last edit: 27.7%); tool-result cap at 1k tokens 14.8% (at 250 tokens 21.2%). Sonnet 5: 3.1% and 4.7%. These are oracles assuming no behaviour change.
build_recommendation: Do not build a memory, skill or workflow library: the evidence for coding agents is at most +4-5 pp success, needs an LLM at runtime, and vanishes under budget matching. Build first the E1 'done' reflex: learn G_test from Drain templates of tool outputs labelled by later edits and hidden-test outcomes, deliver once via PostToolUse additionalContext, and randomise per trigger at 20% withhold for OPE. Expected +6-9% $/task on Haiku-class agents (capture 35-50% of 17.8%), about +1% on Sonnet-class; low-to-moderate confidence it survives a live A/B. Run E2 (Read windowing with a next-action-preservation label) offline only, and ship it only if the net saving after the re-read penalty is 5% or more, since the one billed Claude Code study (2607.12161) found hook compression raised cost 6.8%. Separately, one line of product: recommend a 5-minute cache TTL when the observed inter-request gaps allow it (-12% $ for 1h-cache API users).
